previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with one week of lightheadedness on standing and nausea with wretching but no emesis, in the setting of poor oral intake and an episode of non-bloody diarrhea. In the ED she received intravenous fluids; she remained afebrile and without leukocytosis, with a normal ECG and stable basic labs. She was admitted to the surgical service for observation, continued hydration and symptom control, and glucose monitoring given her history of post-bypass hypoglycemia. Her dizziness and nausea resolved with IV fluids and she tolerated water with stable vital signs, so she was discharged home ambulatory with continuation of her home medications including lansoprazole, rifaximin, and PRN ondansetron, and instructed to follow up with her surgeon and return for recurrent or worsening symptoms.
